summary: Intermittent idle gaps during extended completions cause client-side timeouts for long max_tokens requests
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated client-side timeouts when running extended completion requests (max_tokens >= 150k) with long prompt history. Impact: customer-facing feature degrades (session resets) during multi-minute generations; spikes observed between 2026-03-09T04:00Z and 2026-03-10T06:00Z. Observed behavior: generation starts and streams initial chunks, then stalls with a server-side idle gap (~6-12s) before the next chunk; client eventually closes with timeout and records a 504. This is intermittent (approx 10-15% of long runs) and correlates with requests that cross batching thresholds and kernel-swap events. Customer workaround: reduce max_tokens or split into smaller generation segments. Business impact: enterprise customer has production workflows for medical summarization; repeated timeouts block nightly batch jobs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use RW API with model rw-7b-instruct; 2) Provide ~120k token prompt (long history + system notes) and set max_tokens=160000; 3) Enable streaming; 4) Observe output streaming then pause for ~6-12s before next chunk; 5) Repeat ~10-20 times to reproduce intermittent stalls. Note: reproduction more likely when system load is moderate and batching_enabled=true.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Aisha Kapur: Customer reported ~12% failure rate for nightly summarization job after increasing max_tokens to 160k. They provided request IDs and logs. Asked to triage as P1 because it's impacting scheduled processing.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Eve Chen: Acknowledged. Gathering traces, routing to serving-runtime and infra. Requesting any matching request IDs from customer for correlation.
2026-03-10 11:45 - Customer (CodaHealth Support): Provided 15 request IDs spanning us-west-2 and eu-central-1; noted failures primarily in us-west-2 between 04:00-06:00 UTC.

2026-03-11 08:33 - SRE (Liam O'Neill): Synthetic reproducer run showed idle gap when batch policy waited for min_batch_duration before dispatch; kernel swap added extra latency when batch_size=1. Adding trace links.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Eve Chen: Implementing temporary mitigation to reduce min dispatch timeout for long-session routes and pin model variant to a single kernel to avoid swap. Planning controlled rollout to canary (10% traffic) in us-west-2.
2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer: Confirmed lower reproduction rate on canary traffic; still seeing rare (2-3%) occurrences. Asked for permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Batching policy uses a min wait window that, combined with kernel swap, produces an idle gap large enough for client timeouts when streaming small chunks.
Hypothesis 2: Streaming proxy closes idle connections prematurely when there is a kernel swap or KV cache reload between chunks.
Steps performed: pulled request traces, matched request IDs, replayed a subset in staging under load, toggled batching min_duration and kernel prewarm flags.

Findings: reproduced idle gap when batch_size=1 and min_batch_duration=50ms under kernel swap conditions; kernel_swap added 40-200ms depending on model variant, but when combined with prefetch/backpressure and prefix reassembly it occasionally reached >6s in production due to queuing behind large batched jobs.
Related signals: small spike in streaming-proxy connection resets (metric: stream_conn_reset) correlated to queued kernel swaps; KV cache evictions were not significant during failure windows.
Impact scope: affects long max_tokens requests that produce many small streamed chunks and that hit kernel selection paths that are not prewarmed.
Linked telemetry: trace links and dashboard IDs provided to infra team (dashboard: /confluence/dashboards/streaming-idle-gaps).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation deployed 2026-03-12: reduced min_batch_duration from 50ms to 10ms for long-session route and enabled kernel prewarm for rw-7b-instruct in us-west-2 canary (10% traffic).
Observed effect: reproduction rate dropped from ~12% to ~2-3% on canary. No client-visible errors during 24h canary window for non-customer traffic.

Planned permanent fix: (1) implement adaptive batching that detects long-session streaming and prioritizes continuity over throughput; (2) ensure kernel prewarm on route creation; (3) add streaming-proxy keepalive/test-chunk to prevent idle close during kernel swap. Target ETA: 2026-03-19 for rollout to all us-west-2, then eu-central-1 by 2026-03-22.
Follow-ups: add synthetic tests for long-session streaming to CI, update runbook for support to suggest temporary route override (min_batch_duration) as immediate workaround.
Customer communication: CS to send interim status and ETA for permanent fix; offer assistance in scheduling reduced max_tokens runs as temporary workaround.
notes: Avoided attributing root cause to KV cache eviction; current evidence points to combined effect of batching delay + kernel swap + streaming-proxy idle handling. Monitoring dashboards created and alert thresholds set for stream_conn_reset > 0.5% per minute.
customer_impact_summary: Enterprise nightly jobs intermittently time out and require manual retries; customer requests a permanent fix and timeline to remove workaround.
